newsitem.title: USA: U.S. civil rights group NAACP no longer in debt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. civil rights group NAACP no longer in debt.

text.p: The National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People has paid off debts of $3.2 million and is beginning to rebuild, the head of the nation's oldest civil rights group said Saturday.
NAACP President Kweisi Mfume, a former congressman from Maryland, has spent most of his time revamping the group since taking over as its president in February.

"Effective today, we have paid off all of the existing $3.2 million debt I inherited in February of this year, and the NAACP for the first time in a long time is operating in the black," he told reporters.

The civil rights group has been mired in controversy over its leadership, direction and finances for the past two years, but Mfume said he was rebuilding the organisation's financial reserves and membership was rising.
